title: Critic's Eye: Review-Grounded Graph Reasoning for Long-Form Motif Discovery

body: Deep narrative understanding requires distinguishing what happens from how it is presented, moving beyond the chronological fabula to decode the sjuzet, the discursive organization through which themes are staged. We study this through the recurrence of literary motifs (blood in Macbeth, for instance), where symbolic significance emerges not from local cues, but through repetition-with-variation across the whole work. We operationalize this setting as Computational Motif Discovery, a transductive task that predicts missing line-motif links using the full narrative structure of a play. We propose Critic's Eye, which models the work as a heterogeneous Narrative Topology Graph and performs discriminative inference over global structural evidence. Critic's Eye achieves 84.8% Hit@5 on our benchmark, nearly quadrupling state-of-the-art proprietary foundation models (Gemini-3-pro-preview, ~22.6%). Our analysis reveals that despite massive scaling, sequence-based models hit a "semantic ceiling", struggling to resolve dispersed dependencies. These findings suggest that explicit structural priors are a far more effective inductive bias than parameter scaling for decoding the complex architecture of long-form literature.
summaryZh: 评论家的眼睛：长篇主题发现的基于评论的图形推理。深入的叙事理解需要区分发生的事情和它的呈现方式，超越时间顺序的寓言来解码 sjuzet，即上演主题的话语组织。我们通过文学主题的重复（例如《麦克白》中的血）来研究这一点，其中象征意义不是来自局部线索，而是通过整个作品的重复与变化而出现。
